subject: Re: Request: Network segmentation & attack-surface map for Dedicated/Private deployments

Cc: security@acme-systems.com
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Network segmentation & attack-surface map request for Dedicated/Private

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for taking time to speak earlier. As part of our security intake for the pilot, our InfoSec team has asked for a concise 'attack-surface map' and a network segmentation diagram that shows how Redwood's Dedicated and Private options isolate tenant workloads and management/control planes. Specifically they'd like: 

- A diagram showing control-plane vs data-plane network paths (including VPC peering/eBGP, if applicable)
- How tenant isolation is realized at L2/L3 and at the orchestration layer
- Any east-west microsegmentation / egress controls you enforce for private deployments
- Where audit logs, KMS, and model artifacts transit (and under what encryption/TLS)

Can you share a one-pager plus any supporting artifacts (diagram + CSV of boundary definitions) by next Wednesday? We need something we can attach to our SIG questionnaire.

Appreciate it — cc'ing security@acme-systems.com for context.

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Lee
Senior Security Engineer
Acme Systems

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear ask. I've looped in KarThik and Olga from Architecture & Security who will assemble the diagrams and the boundary table. We'll produce a concise one-pager and the supporting files (PDF diagram + CSV) and post to a shared drive link.

Quick notes on scope so we're aligned: 
- We will provide the logical network diagram (control plane, data plane, optional VPC-on-prem connectivity) and a separate file that enumerates enforced egress rules for Private deployments.
- For Dedicated (reserved capacity) we'll highlight the tenant placement model and how routing is constrained within the dedicated GPU pools.

Can you confirm whether your SIG wants a CAIQ-style mapping or a higher-level diagram only? If you prefer CAIQ mapping, we can produce a short mapping doc but it'll add ~1 business day.

Jonas Weber
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Network segmentation & attack-surface map request for Dedicated/Private deployments

Folks — attaching first-draft artifacts for review.

Attachments: segmentation-diagram-v1.pdf (diagram), network-boundary-table.csv (CSV enumerating subnets, control-plane endpoints, and ACLs)

Summary (TL;DR):
- Control plane is hosted in Redwood-managed control VPCs; management/control traffic is authenticated to customer tenant using mTLS and authorized via tenant-scoped ACLs. Control plane endpoints are accessible only from our private control plane subnets (no public ingress except managed API gateway for hosted customers).
- Data plane for Private deployments: customer-managed VPCs peer to the Redwood data plane via VPC peering or private connectivity (Transit Gateway/Direct Connect equivalents). Tenant compute nodes run in customer subnets or dedicated host pools (depending on deployment).
- Dedicated pools: tenants are placed into isolated GPU pools with enforced network policies; cross-tenant traffic blocked at host-level and via hypervisor/network policy.
- Logs & artifacts: audit logs are forwarded to customer-specified log collectors over TLS 1.3; model artifacts are stored in encrypted object storage with CMK usage logged to KMS audit trails.

Open items for Sarah: 
1) Do you want explicit firewall rule examples (we have a templated set) included in the CSV?
2) Do you require packet-flow-level diagrams (sequence of API calls and ports) or is the logical diagram sufficient for your SIG intake?

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Architect, Infra Security
Redwood Inference

- Please include the templated firewall rule examples in the CSV; we'll use them to validate our compliance scanner.
- For the CAIQ mapping: we only need the network-related controls called out (e.g., SC- network segmentation, boundary protection). The logical diagram + the CSV with example ACLs should be sufficient; CAIQ mapping is optional for now.
- Can you add a short paragraph in the one-pager about how we handle failover and cross-region traffic (if a Private deployment spans regions or if Dedicated capacity fails over to a backup pool)?

If you can get the updated bundle by EOD Monday our compliance review starts Tuesday.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short sync if helpful.

Sarah

Hi Sarah — following up with the finalized bundle and a short executive summary. Deliverables attached.

Attachments: redwood-seg-psa-2026-07-05.pptx (one-pager + executive notes)

Executive summary (for SIG reviewers):
- Separation model: Redwood enforces a strict separation between control and data planes. Control plane components are fully managed by Redwood and do not reside in customer-owned subnets. Data plane connectivity for Private is customer-initiated (peering or private connect) and can be scoped to single-VPC or multi-VPC topologies depending on customer requirements.
- Tenant isolation: For Dedicated customers we use isolated GPU host pools, host-level network policies, and enforced ACLs at the orchestration layer. For Private on-customer-VPC deployments, network isolation is achieved via customer VPC boundaries + Redwood-applied network policies; there is no shared L2 broadcast domain across tenants.
- Failover & cross-region: We support optional cross-region replication of artifacts and an automated failover policy for Dedicated pools (warm standby). Failover traffic to backup pools is tunneled over mTLS + mutual VPN and is subject to the same ACLs and logging controls.

Action items: 
- Karthik/Olga: attach templated firewall rules in the network-boundary-table.csv (done).
- Jonas: confirm the Drive link and ensure the SIG copy is shared with security@acme-systems.com (done).

Next steps: Sarah — I can set up a 30-minute walkthrough Tuesday to step through the diagram and the ACL examples if helpful.

Thanks,
Markus Klein
VP, Product Security
Redwood Inference
